papers.title: On homogeneous hypertournaments
papers.author: Matěj Konečný
papers.description: Pair-cancelling omission classes, even orientations, Ramsey expansions, EPPA and the local constraint hierarchy.

papers.title: Generalised potential structures
papers.author: Matěj Konečný
papers.description: A companion proof for finite involutive raw palettes and finite abelian effective groups.

papers.title: Classification of (n+1)-constrained n-hypertournaments
papers.author: Matěj Konečný
papers.description: The general local amalgamation classification and the five-constrained ternary classification.

entries.title: Intrinsic hypertournaments
entries.scope: An orientation on injective n-tuples, with reversal under every transposition.
entries.notes: The auxiliary linear order is not part of a Hyper structure. The structure is defined in all arities; the paper considers n >= 2.

entries.title: Orientation-preserving embeddings
entries.scope: Arbitrary vertex injections preserve the orientation of every ordered injective tuple.
entries.notes: No vertex-order preservation is imposed. Pullback is the actual induced sub-hypertournament.

entries.title: Forbidden families and omission classes
entries.scope: A family of finite forbidden hypertournaments is represented on each Fin m; omission excludes every intrinsic induced copy.
entries.notes: The family can be infinite. A displayed representative excludes all of its isomorphic copies through arbitrary embeddings.

entries.title: Normalized local index and admissible palettes
entries.scope: On an (n+1)-tuple, normalize the facet orientations by deletion parity and take the minority count.
entries.notes: The allowed-index predicate is on actual local orbit indices. The central index is floor((n+1)/2).

entries.title: Ordinary amalgamation for local classes
entries.scope: The class of finite hypertournaments with all local indices in S has ordinary AP.
entries.notes: Ordinary AP permits extra identifications. Strong AP additionally requires exactly the original overlap. The second declaration is the arbitrary-class strong-AP interface.

entries.title: General finite hereditary classes
entries.scope: Finite presentations carry an arbitrary class predicate, including heredity, unboundedness and class-level ordinary EPPA.
entries.notes: These interfaces are used by the EPPA theorems for classes beyond the local-palette classes.

entries.title: Even hypertournaments
entries.scope: Every injective (n+1)-tuple has zero sum of its raw facet orientations in ZMod 2.
entries.notes: For the potential construction, the upper arity is odd n = r+1 and r is even.

entries.title: An actual alternating potential
entries.scope: The coboundary of the lower-arity hypertournament equals the upper orientation on every tuple.
entries.notes: Lean uses r for the potential arity and r+1 for the original hypertournament arity.

entries.title: Finite EPPA witnesses
entries.scope: Every actual partial automorphism of the source extends to an automorphism of one finite target containing it.
entries.notes: This is ordinary EPPA: extensions of different partial automorphisms are not required to be coherent.

entries.title: Homogeneous intrinsic structures
entries.scope: Any two embeddings of the same finite hypertournament into the structure differ by an actual automorphism.
entries.notes: Quantification over Fin m presentations represents arbitrary finite partial isomorphisms by reindexing.

entries.title: Classes determined by bounded local constraints
entries.scope: KConstrained K k permits any defining forbidden family whose structures all have at most k vertices.
entries.notes: The strict hierarchy excludes every smaller alternative forbidden-family presentation.

entries.label: thm:intro-link
entries.title: Ramsey and ordering properties of pair-cancelling omission classes
entries.scope: For n >= 3, omit any family of finite pair-cancelling n-hypertournaments and add arbitrary vertex orders.
entries.notes: The Ramsey witnesses are finite structures in the actual freely ordered omission class. The ordering witness is fixed before both orders are quantified.

entries.label: thm:potential
entries.title: Ramsey potential expansions of even hypertournaments
entries.scope: For every odd upper arity n >= 3, name an alternating (n-1)-potential and an arbitrary linear order.
entries.notes: Use Lean r = n-1, with Even r and 2 <= r. The expansion-property target is fixed before all source and target potentials and orders.

entries.label: thm:intro-eppa
entries.title: Three introductory non-EPPA conclusions
entries.scope: Unbounded hereditary SAP classes fail EPPA for n >= 6; pair-cancelling omission classes fail EPPA for n >= 4; the class of even 5-hypertournaments fails EPPA.
entries.notes: The first two statements concern ordinary EPPA and use unrestricted finite witness obstructions.

entries.label: lem:local-type-isomorphism
entries.title: The local index completely determines the (n+1)-vertex type
entries.scope: For n >= 2, two n-hypertournaments on n+1 vertices are isomorphic exactly when their local indices agree.
entries.notes: The finite-presentation theorem uses an actual orientation-preserving vertex permutation; every real index is also realized.

entries.label: def:locally-finite
entries.title: Local finiteness for the relational completion theorem
entries.scope: The relational/unary language interface used by the paper checks a completion implication at a fixed local cutoff.
entries.notes: This is the exact native local-finiteness predicate instantiated by the hypertournament adapter; no function symbols occur in its language.

entries.label: thm:HN
entries.title: The locally finite Ramsey-class transfer used here
entries.scope: A finite hereditary strong-amalgamation subclass K, locally finite in a Ramsey ambient class R whose members are irreducible; the application here has a function-free ordered language.
entries.notes: The entry records the proved relational/unary instance needed in this article. The hypertournament language has no functions, and the adapter proves local finiteness with cutoff one.

entries.label: def:pair-cancelling
entries.title: Pair cancellation
entries.scope: Arity n >= 3, at least n+1 vertices, and a nonconstant pair link for every pair and every auxiliary linear order.
entries.notes: The quantified auxiliary order only orders the tuple tail after the two distinguished vertices.

entries.label: lem:local-types
entries.title: Exactly which local types are pair-cancelling
entries.scope: On n+1 vertices with n >= 3, pair cancellation is equivalent to d <= floor((n+1)/2)-2.
entries.notes: Both directions hold for the full arbitrary-auxiliary-order predicate.

entries.label: prop:link-completion
entries.title: Completion of partially prescribed orientations
entries.scope: For n >= 3 and a pair-cancelling forbidden family, arbitrary relational input with an extendible order and admitted irreducible pieces has a completion.
entries.notes: The general conclusion keeps the same carrier and the identity homomorphism-embedding. The intrinsic partial-orientation completion is its core.

entries.label: prop:link-SAP
entries.title: Strong amalgamation of pair-cancelling omission classes
entries.scope: For n >= 3 and any family of finite pair-cancelling forbidden structures, actual finite strong amalgams exist.
entries.notes: Empty bases and arbitrary source embeddings are included; the ordered form preserves both supplied compatible orders.

entries.label: cor:sullivan-ramsey
entries.title: Continuum many homogeneous hypertournaments with Ramsey ages
entries.scope: For each n >= 3, construct continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic countably infinite homogeneous n-hypertournaments whose freely ordered ages are Ramsey with the ordering property.
entries.notes: The finite antichain and countable limits are constructed. The chosen family additionally has no finitely bounded age.

entries.label: lem:alternating-sums
entries.title: Potential existence and switching equivalence
entries.scope: Every finite even odd-arity hypertournament has an alternating potential, and any two potentials differ by a symmetric lower gauge coboundary.
entries.notes: The source upper arity is n = r+1 with Even r and r >= 2. Finite empty carriers are included in these interfaces.

entries.label: prop:potential-SAP
entries.title: Strong amalgamation of potential expansions and even reducts
entries.scope: For odd n >= 3, finite even n-hypertournaments, and their potential-and-order expansions, strongly amalgamate.
entries.notes: A relative gauge aligns potentials over the shared base; the final carrier has exactly the original overlap.

entries.label: prop:higharity-eppa-obstruction
entries.title: The local obstruction to unrestricted finite EPPA witnesses
entries.scope: For n >= 4, two (n+1)-packets agree on an n-point base, have distinct extra vertices, and admit four equal normalized base facets.
entries.notes: No orientation involving both extra vertices is prescribed. The obstruction excludes every finite target, including unrestricted hypertournaments on arbitrary finite carriers.

entries.label: lem:klein-centralizer-generation
entries.title: Generation by centralizers under a Klein-four action
entries.scope: A Klein four-group acts by automorphisms on a finite odd-order group; elements fixed by nonidentity acting elements generate the whole group.
entries.notes: The group-theoretic generation assertion itself is proved, with arbitrary Klein-four groups rather than chosen generators.

entries.label: thm:higharity-no-eppa
entries.title: Non-EPPA for general hereditary SAP classes and PC omission classes
entries.scope: For a hereditary strong-amalgamation class: when n >= 6, unboundedness implies failure of EPPA; when n >= 4, it suffices to contain a packet with local index d <= n-3. For n >= 4, every omission class of pair-cancelling structures fails EPPA.
entries.notes: The common PC-family obstruction has exactly n+2 vertices and has no finite EPPA witness even in the unrestricted class. The criterion includes d = q-1.

entries.label: prop:even-eppa-transfer
entries.title: EPPA descends one arity
entries.scope: For odd n >= 3, EPPA for the even n-ary class or the unrestricted n-ary class implies EPPA for all (n-1)-hypertournaments.
entries.notes: The reduction constructs an even one-point cone and recovers the source as the link of the distinguished vertex.

entries.label: cor:even-no-eppa
entries.title: Even odd-arity classes from arity five have no EPPA
entries.scope: For odd n >= 5, the class of finite even n-hypertournaments fails ordinary EPPA.
entries.notes: The arity-five instance is also exported separately.

entries.label: def:generalised-potential
entries.title: Generalised potential structures
entries.scope: Fix finite Q with an involution, finite abelian G, a surjective equivariant effective map, and offset a = 0 in even upper arity; effective labels are closed.
entries.notes: Raw labels, not only effective group values, are preserved. Lean uses potential arity r and upper arity r+1. The full companion crosswalk is on the generalised-potential page.

entries.label: thm:affine-labelled
entries.title: SAP and precompact Ramsey expansions for generalised potentials
entries.scope: Under Definition 6.1, every finite closed raw structure has a potential, the reduct class has SAP, and naming a potential and free order gives a precompact Ramsey expansion with the expansion property.
entries.notes: Noninjective effective maps and involution-fixed raw labels are allowed. The expansion-property target is fixed before every later potential and order choice; fixed raw labels survive the decoding.

entries.label: thm:constrained-classification
entries.title: Complete unbounded local classification and strong AP
entries.scope: For n >= 4, S contains the central type and contains only real local indices; AP holds exactly for the next-central or odd switching alternatives. The low arities n=2,3 also satisfy AP implies SAP for unbounded classes.
entries.notes: Indices represent the source orbit types T_(n,d). The companion classification supplement gives the negative proof and the separate at-most-five ternary classification.

entries.label: obs:strict-constrained-hierarchy
entries.title: A strict hierarchy of local constraint levels
entries.scope: For every k > n >= 3, one actual k-vertex pair-cancelling obstruction defines an unbounded hereditary SAP class that is k-constrained and is not (k-1)-constrained.
entries.notes: Every requested size is realized, including sizes below the cycle-antichain bound. The negation rules out every alternative forbidden-family presentation using smaller structures.

entries.title: Fixed raw palette and effective group data
entries.scope: An involutive raw palette Q, an additive commutative group G, an offset a, and a surjective equivariant map Q → G.
entries.notes: The paper assumes finite Q and G. The data structures themselves do not impose finiteness or exclude involution-fixed labels. For upper arity n the parity condition is a = 0 when n is even.

entries.title: Tuple labels and raw-label embeddings
entries.scope: Labels are assigned to injective ordered tuples; odd coordinate permutations apply the palette involution.
entries.notes: An embedding preserves every original Q-label. Equality of effective group labels alone is not the embedding condition.

entries.label: def:potential-structures
entries.title: Generalised potential structures and chosen potentials
entries.scope: For raw arity n = r+1, Closed means δ(η∘ω)=0, and IsPotential means δp=η∘ω for an affine alternating r-ary p.
entries.notes: The paper's n is one more than the potential arity r used by Expansion. Ordinary signed gauges use offset zero; they are not affine gauges with offset a.

entries.title: Actual potential-and-order expansions
entries.scope: An expansion names the raw Q-labels and one compatible potential; a free linear order is added in the native relational language.
entries.notes: Expansion.Preserves retains both raw and potential labels. Native ordered embeddings additionally preserve the named order.

entries.title: The signed coboundary and its permutation law
entries.scope: Cochains take values in an arbitrary additive commutative group. Under the zero-offset condition in even upper arity, an affine coboundary has the required affine permutation law.
entries.notes: This covers equation (1), δ²=0, and the symmetry calculation preceding the cone lemma. The signs are integral ±1 coefficients; characteristic two is not assumed.

entries.label: thm:main
entries.title: Strong amalgamation and a precompact Ramsey expansion
entries.scope: Upper arity n≥3; fixed finite Q and finite abelian G; η is equivariant and surjective, with a=0 when n is even; all vertex carriers in the classes are finite.
entries.notes: The six declarations prove the theorem's components for actual raw structures and actual expansions. Set Lean r=n−1; the hypothesis Even (r+1) → d.offset=0 is exactly the paper's parity condition.

entries.label: lem:cone
entries.title: Cone contraction and signed exactness
entries.scope: An ordinary alternating closed cochain in arity k≥2 over an additive commutative group is a signed coboundary.
entries.notes: The existential theorem works in every positive degree, without a finite-carrier or carrier-order assumption. The second declaration identifies the explicit contraction when a root is chosen.

entries.label: lem:potentials
entries.title: Potential existence and switching by a signed gauge
entries.scope: Finite closed raw structures have affine potentials. Two potentials of the same structure differ by the signed coboundary of an ordinary alternating lower cochain.
entries.notes: The first result is an iff. The gauge theorem and its converse retain the same raw structure, including noninjective effective maps and raw-label fibres.

entries.label: prop:sap
entries.title: Strong amalgamation of reducts and expansions
entries.scope: Fixed affine data and the arity parity condition; finite side carriers; raw arity at least three for the reduct theorem.
entries.notes: The witnesses live on the explicit exact-overlap carrier. The ordered theorem retains both given side orders. These amalgamation results do not require finiteness of Q or G.

entries.title: Reasonableness of the expansion
entries.scope: A potential and order on a finite source extend along a prescribed raw embedding into a fixed larger finite closed raw structure.
entries.notes: This is the reasonableness paragraph after Proposition 3.1. The target raw structure and the original vertex injection stay fixed while its potential and order are chosen.

entries.label: prop:ramsey
entries.title: Ramsey property in the original expanded language
entries.scope: Fixed affine data satisfying the arity parity condition; finite ordered inputs and any finite nonempty colour palette.
entries.notes: The Ramsey witness names the original raw labels, a compatible potential and a free order. The arrow itself works without finiteness of Q or G; those hypotheses are used elsewhere for precompactness and the full expansion-property argument.

entries.label: lem:ordering
entries.title: Ordering property for a fixed potential-expanded structure
entries.scope: Potential arity r≥2 and a finite actual expansion (raw,p).
entries.notes: The finite target raw/potential expansion is chosen before both the source order and target order. Thus every order of the fixed target contains every ordered expansion of the source.

entries.label: prop:expansion
entries.title: Full expansion property relative to the raw class
entries.scope: Potential arity r≥2, finite Q and G, fixed affine data, and a finite closed raw source.
entries.notes: One finite closed raw target is fixed before both potentials and both orders are quantified. The embeddings preserve raw labels as well as the chosen potentials and orders.

entries.title: Precompactness and the finite expansion signature
entries.scope: A finite effective group and finite vertex carrier give finitely many potential-and-order expansions of a fixed raw structure; finite Q also gives a finite signature.
entries.notes: Finiteness is proved on the fixed carrier before quotienting by isomorphism. The expanded language introduces relations, not function symbols.

entries.title: Decoding raw fibres with fixed upper codes
entries.scope: Arbitrary surjective effective maps, including fibres with several raw labels.
entries.notes: This is the implementation bridge used in the Ramsey and expansion-property proofs. A fixed upper code still decodes to the same raw target after its compatible potential changes; unique codes are not assumed.

entries.title: The arity-dependent drift of a homogeneous gauge
entries.scope: Ordinary signed lower gauges over an additive commutative group, homogeneous on increasing tuples.
entries.notes: These are the drift calculations in equations (5), (6) and (11). The drift vanishes in even potential arity and may be nonzero in odd potential arity, which is why even upper arity needs the additional correction.

entries.title: Recovery of even hypertournaments
entries.scope: Q=G=ZMod 2 with complementary raw labels, offset 1, identity effective map and odd upper arity.
entries.notes: Signed and unsigned coboundaries coincide over ZMod 2. The bridge identifies the original evenness and potential equations, and preserves the original intrinsic embeddings.

entries.label: lem:local-types
entries.title: Local types are classified by the minority index
entries.scope: For n ≥ 2, two n-hypertournaments on n+1 vertices are isomorphic exactly when their local indices agree; every d ≤ floor((n+1)/2) is realized.
entries.notes: The isomorphism is an actual orientation-preserving permutation, not merely an equality of packet counts.

entries.label: lem:unbounded
entries.title: Unboundedness is equivalent to allowing the central type
entries.scope: For any arity n and local-index palette S, UnboundedAdmissible n S holds exactly when centralIndex n belongs to S.
entries.notes: Unboundedness means existence of finite members of arbitrarily large cardinality.

entries.label: thm:main-classification
entries.title: Complete unbounded local-palette amalgamation classification
entries.scope: For n ≥ 4 and a valid palette containing q=floor((n+1)/2), AP holds exactly when q−1 is allowed, or n is odd and S is the even/switching palette. Every positive case has SAP. For n=2,3 every central-containing palette has SAP.
entries.notes: The all-arities interface assumes n ≥ 2 and records the small-arity alternative n ≤ 3 explicitly. ValidTypes restricts indices to actual local types. The AP-to-SAP corollary only assumes unboundedness, so irrelevant indices above q need not be removed first.

entries.label: thm:classification
entries.title: Every excluded palette has an ordinary one-point obstruction
entries.scope: For n ≥ 4, a valid central-containing palette omitting q−1 fails ordinary AP unless n is odd and it is the even/switching palette.
entries.notes: The first declaration is the unconditional public non-AP theorem. The one-point formulation is assembled by applying the displayed induction reduction to oddToggleOnePointObstructions_of_p3 p3OddOnePointObstructions. The two reduction lemmas have explicit hypotheses; the final displayed p3 theorem discharges them. Ordinary AP allows identification of the new vertices and targets larger than the union of the two sides.

entries.label: lem:local-pc
entries.title: Which local types are pair-cancelling
entries.scope: For n ≥ 3, a structure on n+1 vertices is pair-cancelling exactly when its local index is at most centralIndex n − 2.
entries.notes: This identifies the first positive alternative with omission of pair-cancelling forbidden structures.

entries.label: prop:pc-sap
entries.title: Strong amalgamation by a constant mixed link
entries.scope: For n ≥ 3, omitting any family of pair-cancelling finite n-hypertournaments admits strong amalgamation along arbitrary finite spans.
entries.notes: The concrete span theorem preserves the given injections and introduces no extra overlap.

entries.label: lem:exactness
entries.title: Elementary exactness of Boolean cochains
entries.scope: A cochain closed in the next degree is the coboundary of its contraction at a chosen vertex; this provides the potentials used for odd-arity even hypertournaments.
entries.notes: The cochain theorem takes an actual root a : V. The finite hypertournament potential equivalence handles the carrier cases internally and does not require nonemptiness. No external cohomology theorem is needed.

entries.label: prop:even-sap
entries.title: Strong amalgamation of even hypertournaments
entries.scope: In odd arity n ≥ 3, even hypertournaments have strong amalgamation by gluing compatible potentials of arity n−1.
entries.notes: The ordered version also retains the prescribed orders on the two sides.

entries.label: lem:4-central
entries.title: The central-only arity-four seed
entries.scope: The palette {2} in arity four has a finite bad ordinary one-point span, hence fails AP.
entries.notes: The explicit seed is checked in the intrinsic orientation language; distinct side orientations also exclude identifying the two new vertices.

entries.label: lem:4-forb
entries.title: The arity-four seed omitting the middle type
entries.scope: The palette {0,2} in arity four has a bad ordinary one-point span, hence fails AP.
entries.notes: The checked finite contradiction supplies the same mathematical seed as the supplement's implication tables.

entries.label: lem:zero-two
entries.title: The zero-or-two principle
entries.scope: For n ≡ 1 mod 4 and n ≥ 5, in the even palette enlarged by the homogeneous type, each n+2 vertex set contains zero or exactly two homogeneous n+1 vertex subsets.
entries.notes: This is a statement about actual local packets of an intrinsic hypertournament, rather than an independently prescribed homogeneous-set indicator.

entries.label: lem:5-two
entries.title: The homogeneous-or-central arity-five seed
entries.scope: The arity-five palette {0,3} has a bad ordinary one-point span.
entries.notes: This finite seed is kept separate from both the central-only cone seed and the exceptional {0,1,3} seed.

entries.label: prop:cone
entries.title: Coning a central-only obstruction
entries.scope: The source transfers a central-only even-arity obstruction to the next odd arity; Lean uses the concrete arity-four to arity-five cone seed in the negative classification.
entries.notes: The generic one-arity cone constructor in the source is not separately exported. The checked concrete cone seed and two-step suspension induction establish all central-only non-AP cases needed for the final theorem. The public non-AP theorem is a classification consequence, not the generic cone construction itself.

entries.label: lem:reflection
entries.title: Two-coordinate reflection of an amalgam
entries.scope: Exact recovery of the two lower sides from every pair of pads, together with a sufficiently large pad set, turns any higher amalgam into a lower one; lower side disagreement excludes identification.
entries.notes: Lean records profiles over all ordered injective tuples and assumes |P| > 2^card(Fin(n+1) ↪ Fin(a+2)), where a is the lower base size. The source's sharper 2^(choose(a,n−1)) threshold is not the literal theorem exported here. Both bounds give the qualitative obstruction transfer. The no-joint helper is supplemented by the ordinary-AP theorem, which handles identification.

entries.label: lem:even-types
entries.title: Local types in the even suspension
entries.scope: For source arity 2k, a packet with two pads has old index plus one; all other pad occupancies have the new central index k+1.
entries.notes: Packet calculations use increasing tuples; the admissibility theorem transfers them to arbitrary enumerations through local-index invariance.

entries.label: prop:even-lift
entries.title: Raising an even-arity obstruction by two
entries.scope: A bad one-point span in source arity 2k transfers to arity 2k+2 if the old central index is allowed, the target admits all shifted old indices, and shifting the target back gives only allowed old indices.
entries.notes: This includes both source targets S+ and S+ enlarged by index zero. The construction uses the larger formal reflection bound described above.

entries.label: rem:core
entries.title: A contradiction core can reduce the pad count
entries.scope: The source observes that h relevant mixed sets suffice for a pad set of size 2^h+1.
entries.notes: The formal proof uses the complete ordered-tuple profile, not a selected contradiction core. The optimized numerical bound 2^h+1 is not separately formalized; no classification result depends on this optimization.

entries.label: lem:odd-root
entries.title: The rooted potential identity
entries.scope: The source's signed root identity controls the three-pad packets of the odd suspension.
entries.notes: Lean splits the calculation into root erasure laws and exact packet/local-index identities. It does not export the source's signed integer boundary identity as a standalone equation. The root is chosen first in the old order; the final odd suspension theorem handles the root choice.

entries.label: lem:odd-types
entries.title: Local types in the rooted odd suspension
entries.scope: Two-pad packets and root-absent three-pad packets shift an old local index by one; root-present three-pad packets, four-pad packets, and the remaining occupancies have the new central index.
entries.notes: The root has value zero in the canonical old presentation. The final admissibility statement is intrinsic and quantifies over all injective tuples.

entries.label: thm:odd-lift
entries.title: Raising an odd-arity obstruction by two
entries.scope: For source arity 2k+1 with k ≥ 1, a bad one-point span transfers to arity 2k+3 under the same central and shift conditions as the even lift, using the rooted suspension.
entries.notes: The explicit-span helper assumes a nonempty common base; the final HasBadOnePoint theorem derives the needed base nonemptiness from the obstruction. The reflected contradiction rules out ordinary amalgams.

entries.label: thm:p3
entries.title: The exceptional family in arities congruent to three modulo four
entries.scope: For every k ≥ 1, arity 4k+3 with palette toggleZero(switchingAllowed(4k+3)) has a bad ordinary one-point span.
entries.notes: This is the even/switching palette with the homogeneous type removed. The finite counting construction discharges the exceptional-family hypothesis of the induction; there is no remaining probabilistic assumption.

entries.label: lem:p3-admissible
entries.title: Every assignment produces admissible exceptional sides
entries.scope: For k ≥ 1, positive block size, and arbitrary potential coefficients, both complementary-half one-point sides in the arity-4k+3 construction are admissible.
entries.notes: Admissibility includes nontransversal packets and arbitrary vertex enumerations. These are side-membership lemmas; the non-amalgamation conclusion is the separate theorem above.

entries.label: lem:p3-polarity
entries.title: A unique endpoint bit makes an alternating transversal bad
entries.scope: After fixing an alternating interior packet and its link bits, exactly one remaining common endpoint bit makes the full packet homogeneous.
entries.notes: The probabilistic existence argument is implemented by exact finite counts and the later simultaneous gauge-counting argument, rather than by introducing an independence assumption for synthetic packets.

entries.label: lem:p1-sides
entries.title: Admissibility of the exceptional one-modulo-four sides
entries.scope: For each arity 4k+5, the two explicitly constructed one-point sides belong to the even/switching palette enlarged by the homogeneous type.
entries.notes: These certify the sides; the next theorem supplies the actual failure of ordinary amalgamation.

entries.label: thm:p1
entries.title: The exceptional family in arities congruent to one modulo four
entries.scope: For every k ≥ 0, arity 4k+5 with palette toggleZero(switchingAllowed(4k+5)) has a bad ordinary one-point span and fails AP.
entries.notes: Here toggling index zero adds the homogeneous type to the even/switching palette.

entries.title: Separate four- and five-vertex prescriptions
entries.scope: Constrained four five combines independent four-vertex local-index bits and five-vertex isomorphism-type bits; normalizedClass five uses exactly the four-types occurring in its allowed five-types.
entries.notes: The five-type palette is a twelve-bit integer. A normalized presentation can impose a genuine condition on four vertices, even when described using its five-palette alone.

entries.label: lem:five-normalization
entries.title: Unbounded amalgamation forces normalization
entries.scope: A consistent unbounded class with separate four/five prescriptions and ordinary AP admits precisely the four-types in the support of its five-palette.
entries.notes: Consistency ensures the support is contained in the prescribed four-types. AP over the empty structure and actual unboundedness give the reverse inclusion.

entries.title: Unboundedness for the finite ternary census
entries.scope: A normalized five-palette is unbounded exactly when bit zero, the constant-orientation type P0, is admitted; the separate-prescription theorem additionally requires the constant-orientation four-type.
entries.notes: This reduces the valid normalized unbounded census to exactly 2048 palettes.

entries.label: thm:five-classification
entries.title: The five normalized ternary amalgamation classes
entries.scope: For a valid twelve-bit normalized palette and an actually unbounded class, AP holds exactly for masks 1,119,257,3583,4095; AP and SAP agree. The consistent separate four/five formulation also requires normalization.
entries.notes: The masks represent cyclic orders (1), H4-free (119), even (257), P9-free (3583), and unrestricted (4095). The numerical ordering in the theorem differs from the display order of the human table. These are normalized four/five classes, not literal five-only classes.

entries.label: rem:five-only
entries.title: Only two classes survive literal five-only constraints
entries.scope: When every four-vertex structure is admitted, a valid unbounded five-only class has AP exactly for masks 3583 and 4095, namely P9-free and unrestricted; both have SAP.
entries.notes: Conditions on five vertices are vacuous on smaller carriers. Thus the first three normalized positive cases cannot be treated as positive literal five-only classes.

entries.title: The twelve five-types and the positive-sign dictionary
entries.scope: The twelve representative masks classify actual five-vertex isomorphism types. Translating the source's positive-sign masks to literal Lean Boolean masks complements the ten bits and permutes type labels by (3 7)(10 11).
entries.notes: This corresponds to the five-type table and the formalization appendix. The dictionary is witnessed by actual preserving vertex permutations. It fixes P9, all four-type supports, and each of the five positive palettes.

entries.title: Complete checked coverage of the 2043 negative palettes
entries.scope: Among the 2048 normalized palettes containing P0, every nonpositive palette is blocked by one of 37 concrete checked one-point diagrams; each checked bounded diagram excludes actual ordinary AP.
entries.notes: Coverage and soundness are separate proofs. Soundness uses intrinsic embeddings, permits vertex identification, and rules out larger amalgam targets by restricting to the union of the two images. These claims do not rely on an external search program being trusted.

entries.title: The P9-free class has SAP, Ramsey expansions, and the ordering property
entries.scope: The five-vertex structure P9 is pair-cancelling. Its omission class has strong amalgamation; freely ordered finite members form a Ramsey class and satisfy the ordering property.
entries.notes: These are applications of the main article's general pair-cancelling completion theorems to the new positive example in the supplement. The ordering theorem quantifies over every subsequently chosen pair of free linear orders.
